Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck
pain, stiffness, and intermittent headache. The mechanism of injury is consistent with
the reported symptoms, and the presentation is in keeping with a cervical strain. Care
was delivered over 22 visits, which is somewhat longer than typical for this injury,
and progress was gradual with ongoing reports of discomfort. Physical examination
findings were limited, and the primary basis for the clinical picture is the patient's
own description of pain and its effect on daily activity. Cervical imaging was
reviewed and showed no acute abnormality, and provocative orthopedic tests were
negative. The patient reports a remote, minor strain to the same region in the past
that resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing records were reviewed and
reflect single entries for each service without duplicate charges. Ongoing management
includes home stretching, activity modification, and as-needed analgesia, with
reassessment planned to determine whether further visits are warranted.
